raw_text:
Here is a concise, integrated 12-week postpartum plan summary, combining Phase structure, weekly cadence, cardio, HIIT considerations, core/abs progression, strength progression, and breastfeeding nutrition notes. It’s written as a trainer-ready overview you can hand to your client or load into your plan doc. If you’d like, I can convert this into a printable week-by-week sheet with fields for sets/reps/weights and symptom notes.

Overall structure at a glance
- Phases
  - Phase 1: Recovery Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
  - Phase 2: Six-Week Readiness (Weeks 5–6)
  - Phase 3: Progressive Return with Strength Emphasis (Weeks 7–12)
- Weekly cadence
  - 3 strength/specific conditioning sessions per week on non-consecutive days
  - 1–2 optional daily mobility/breathing sessions
  - Cardio: light to moderate progression integrated through all phases, with HIIT considered only if criteria are met (Weeks 9–12 window recommended with caution)
- Core and pelvic floor
  - Priority on pelvic floor activation, diaphragmatic breathing, and diastasis monitoring
  - Abs work introduced carefully starting Week 5, progressing to more targeted core and anti-rotation/anti-extension work by Weeks 7–12
- Breastfeeding considerations
  - Adequate protein, hydration, and calories
  - Balance workouts with lactation needs; adjust intensity if milk supply or energy is affected

Phase 1: Recovery Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Objectives
- Establish pelvic floor awareness, diaphragmatic breathing, neutral spine control
- Gentle hip/ankle mobility; no abdominal loading or heavy lifting
- Begin walking; energy permitting, accumulate daily steps

Structure
- Sessions: 3 per week (A/B split, non-consecutive), plus optional daily mobility/breathing
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes
- Core focus: diaphragmatic breathing with pelvic floor activation; avoid doming; no loaded abs
- Core/low-load progressions: gentle dead-bug progressions, rib control with breath
- Strength moves (no heavy load): glute bridges, clam shells (no resistance), bird-dogs (modified if needed)
- Walking: start 15–20 minutes, progressing toward 20–30 minutes as tolerated
- Global cues: ribcage down, pelvic floor up on exhale, breath synchronized with movement

Phase 2: Six-Week Readiness (Weeks 5–6)
Objectives
- Reintroduce light resistance with safe core activation
- Protect pelvic floor; monitor diastasis
- Prepare for more structured loading after six-week clearance

Structure
- Sessions: 3 per week
- Core focus: dead bugs with progressions, supine bracing with rib control, elevated planks if cleared
- Resistance introduction: light bands or light dumbbells for rows, hip hinges to chair, glute bridges with tempo
- Movement variety: standing balance, wall presses, side-lying hip work
- Walking/cardio: 20–30 minutes daily if energy allows; post-six-week clearance optional very light cardio intervals (1 minute brisk, 1–2 minutes easy) totaling 15–20 minutes

Phase 3: Progressive Return with Strength Emphasis (Weeks 7–12)
Objectives
- Build strength, stability, and conditioning with progressive overload
- Safe loading patterns for squats, hinges, pushes, pulls, and anti-rotation/core work
- Integrate cardio and, if appropriate, HIIT with strict safety criteria

Structure
- Sessions: 3 strength days per week (non-consecutive)
- Core progression: from braced dead bugs and Pallof press to more demanding planks/regression as tolerated
- Strength progression framework
  - Weeks 7–8: foundation of heavier loading with tempo and technique emphasis
  - Weeks 9–10: intensified loading, tempo manipulation, increased volume
  - Weeks 11–12: near-peak loads with controlled testing and confidence checks
- Sample main lifts (progressive overload targets; adjust to client equipment)
  - Goblet squats, hip thrusts, Romanian deadlifts, bent-over rows, incline push-ups, floor/bench presses, single-arm rows, overhead carries
  - Core: Pallof press, dead bugs with tempo, side planks with regression, anti-extension/anti-rotation variations
- Cardio progression
  - Phase 1: daily 15–25 min walks
  - Phase 2: 2–3 cardio sessions of 12–20 min
  - Phase 3: 2–3 cardio sessions 20–30 min; add one longer session (25–40 min) by Weeks 11–12
  - Modality: walking, cycling, elliptical, swimming; avoid high-impact or improper intra-abdominal loading
- HIIT (consideration)
  - Best introduced only if Week 9–10 with clinician clearance, pelvic floor stability, and diastasis control
  - Start with 4–6 rounds of 20s light effort / 40–60s easy; no more than 1 HIIT session per week initially
  - If any leakage, doming, pain, or fatigue spikes occur, revert to low-intensity cardio
- Nutrition/Recovery alignment
  - Protein target: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day
  - Calorie target: modest surplus or maintenance for lactation (~300–500 kcal/day above pre-pregnancy maintenance, adjust by hunger)
  - Hydration: 3–3.5 L/day plus extra around feeds/workouts
  - Sleep and stress management: prioritize baby sleep scaffolding, short naps when possible
- Diastasis and pelvic floor checks
  - Throughout Weeks 7–12, monitor midline stability during braced/core work
  - If doming or leakage worsens, regress to safer core progressions and consult pelvic floor PT

Weekly structure (example week-by-week outline)
- Week 1–2 (Phase 1)
  - Session A: diaphragmatic breathing + pelvic floor activation, light bridging, cat-cow, hip mobility
  - Session B: seated leg slides, hip abduction, wall angels, marching
  - Optional short daily mobility/breathing
- Week 3–4 (Phase 1 continuation)
  - Session A: breathing + pelvic floor, light glute bridges, clamshells (no resistance), prone cobra/cobra, hamstring glides
  - Session B: standing marching, side-lying leg lifts, bird-dog (modified), monster walks, mobility circuit
- Week 5–6 (Phase 2)
  - Session A: dead bugs, bracing, glute bridges with tempo, clamshells with light band (if tolerable)
  - Session B: single-leg balance with light reach, light band rows, wall press, hip hinge to chair, core integration
- Week 7–12 (Phase 3)
  - Week 7–8: 3 strength sessions with progressive load, 2–3 core moves per session, 15–25 min cardio
  - Week 9–10: heavier loads, tempo variations; add 1 HIIT option if clearance/comfort
  - Week 11–12: peak strength with 1–2 heavier sets for main lifts, 3–4 core moves, 25–40 min cardio; consider a mild endurance test or performance check
- Daily mobility/breathing: 5–10 minutes, including diaphragmatic breathing, rib control, hip/opening stretches

Nutrition integration for breastfeeding
- Protein: distribute 25–35 g per main meal plus snacks; total 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day
- Hydration: 3.0–3.5 L/day baseline; add 1 cup per breastfeeding session
- Calorie strategy: aim for a modest surplus or maintenance
- Micro-nutrients: emphasize calcium, iron, iodine, omega-3s (DHA), vitamin D as needed
- Pre-/post-workout fueling: balanced snack before workouts; protein-rich meal within 1–2 hours post-workout
- Convenience: batch meals, batch-cook proteins/grains, keep ready-to-eat options

Equipment and safety notes
- Equipment: mat, bands (light–medium), dumbbells (as available), chair/bench
- Diastasis checks: trainer to monitor; regression if doming present
- Pelvic floor cues: instruct pelvic floor lifts before, during, and after all movements
- Red flags: persistent leakage, pain, doming, back pain or fatigue beyond typical postpartum adaptation; seek clinician or PT input

Measurement and progression tracking
- Symptom log: leakage, doming, pain, fatigue, sleep
- Performance log: weight/reps/sets, RPE, technique quality
- Biweekly or weekly check-ins to adjust volume/load
- Optional lactation endpoint: milk supply perception, infant satiety and growth

Would you like me to format this into:
- A printable one-page 12-week plan with the exact week-by-week exercise names, reps, sets, and load targets tailored to typical equipment, or
- A spreadsheet-ready version with separate tabs for Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3, cardio HIIT options, and nutrition notes?
